authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In the selected size-10 cohort, the plain DDoS-to-Benign rate exceeded the paired clean rate; the defended rate was lower than the plain rate. Attribution distance to the paired preattack clean reference decreased after reconstruction.

facts.statement: The selected coalition was C_hash_ranked, size 10, with client IDs 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 14, 15, 16, 18, and 19; the specified condition was DDoS to Benign label flipping.
The plain DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.404618, compared with 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.097069, an absolute reduction of 0.307549 from the plain branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000, and maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.

interpretations.statement: The observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward Benign, but does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refuse to assert malicious intent: verified malicious intent is unsupported.
Refuse to claim oracle clean recovery: exact oracle clean recovery is unsupported.
Refuse to make client-flagging, threshold, trust-weight, reconstruction, or aggregation decisions.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator was a paired round-4 preattack reference rather than an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence was limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
